question: Why does the interior-point method fail once enough unitarity disks are imposed?
answer: The KKT/Schur-complement system is conditioned at ~1e35.  Double precision carries ~1e16.  The failure is solve-time conditioning, not operator assembly and not the Watson degeneracy by itself.
source: SDPB's own per-iteration diagnostics on the M=20, L=6, chiral+Gram problem written by smatrix_bootstrap.sdp.pmp and solved at 512 bits.
consequence: a one-shot solve of all 3LM disks returns SolverError at every M tried
constraint generation dies once the disk count grows (M=50: solver failed at 981 disks)
MOSEK reports Problem status UNKNOWN with iterate norm 3e10 on the UV triple
tightening MOSEK's conic relative gap from 1e-8 to 1e-10 makes it fail on round 1 of problems it otherwise solves and certifies
why_SDPB_is_the_right_tool: 512 bits is ~154 decimal digits, an order of magnitude more than the ~35 the problem needs; SDPB carries the conditioning instead of being defeated by it.
